[[File:Scott Lingrell 2015 Hall of Fame.jpg|thumb|right|260px|[[Hall of Fame]] class of 2015.]]
'''Scott Lingrell''' ([[GEMP]] handle '''advocate'''; also '''crngwell'''; Players Committee forum handle '''CRingwell'''<ref name="pcf-6375-88430">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=88430#88430 A Recap and more questions.], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 July 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618064056/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=89004 Internet Archive]</ref>)<ref name="yt">[https://www.youtube.com/@crngwell @crngwell] on YouTube. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260927195243/https://www.youtube.com/@crngwell Wayback 27 September 2026]</ref> is the current [[Lead Advocate]] of the [[Players Committee]]. He was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]] (Rogue 60).<ref name="slack-lingrell-2026">Star Wars CCG Slack, #swccgdiscussion, Scott Lingrell, 9 October 2026. "Also, it's not complete. I was gold 60 I think. Rogue 60 sorry"</ref> He organized the Decipher-oriented convention [[RamapoCon III]], held 7–10 June 2001 at Ramapo College in Mahwah, New Jersey, after two years of conventions there.<ref name="ramapo3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20071217070344/http://www.swccgpc.com/ramapocon/index.html RamapoCon 3], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 17 December 2007)</ref> He volunteered for the Players Committee in 2002, including running a Classic Format playtest at DecipherCon 2002.<ref name="dcon2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106101746/http://www.swccgpc.com/ The SWCCG Player's Committee], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 6 November 2002; news dated 29 October 2002)</ref> ''The Ringer'' reported that he joined the committee in 2004.<ref name="ringer">[https://www.theringer.com/2018/05/21/star-wars/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community The Force Is Strong With This 'Star Wars' Subculture], Ben Lindbergh, ''The Ringer'' (21 May 2018). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20250524105937/https://www.theringer.com/2018/05/21/star-wars/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community Wayback 24 May 2025]</ref> He later called the [[2014 Virtual Card Pool Reset]] the best thing the committee could have done.<ref name="ringer" /> The first dated Advocate Council snapshot that names him is 29 August 2005, as Card Design Advocate.<ref name="council2005">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050829220138/http://www.swccgpc.com/council.htm Advocate Council], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 29 August 2005)</ref> The same page places him in Fairless Hills, Pennsylvania, and names him as a liaison with [[DeckTech|DeckTech Players Network]].<ref name="council2005" /> He later served as [[Design Advocate]] and then as Lead Advocate.<ref name="hof">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20200628022310/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Wayback 28 June 2020]</ref> He was in the final eight of the 2001 World Championship ([[FreedomCon]]).<ref name="fc-forum">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=75427 SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History], forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020; players' recollection of the 2001 top 8). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html Internet Archive]</ref> The community gave him a Lifetime Achievement Award in 2011, and the Players Committee enshrined him in the Hall of Fame on 8 August 2015.<ref name="hof" />

== Players Committee work ==

In September 2003, after [[Andrew Howard]] stepped down, [[Michael Pistone]] nominated Lingrell on the Players Committee forum to fill Howard's position as Tournament Advocate.<ref name="pcf-2188-33226">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=33226#33226 New Tournament Advocate], Pistone84, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (17 September 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040112231657/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=36534%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> Before the [[2004 New Jersey Open Qualifier]], which he directed on 14 August 2004, Lingrell announced an auction during the day of signed cards, RamapoCon 3 and tournament t-shirts, uncut sheets and cards, with all the money going to the Players Committee for future expenses and prize money.<ref name="pcf-3634-51976">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=51976#51976 Updated - Open Qualifier 8/14/04 in New Jersey], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (4 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040819030114/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=50430%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> A "Gauntlet" side event he had planned for the day before, in which players would try to beat [[Chris Gogolen]], [[Greg Shaw]] and a third player using random decks, was cancelled because of scheduling conflicts.<ref name="pcf-3634-51901">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=51901#51901 Updated - Open Qualifier 8/14/04 in New Jersey], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (2 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040819030114/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=50430%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

On 18 February 2005, after he became Design Advocate, a forum poster listed cards he had heard Lingrell created; Lingrell denied the others but wrote of [[Asteroid Sanctuary]]: "Sanctuary = that was definately me".<ref name="pcf-4613-63182">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=63182#63182 New Design Advocate!], Scott Lingrell (CRingwell), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (18 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050416235209/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=63182%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

In May 2005, as Design Advocate, Lingrell asked players on the Players Committee forum what would make the game more enjoyable; he wanted feedback on prizes, ratings, tournament resources, events and the ease of use of the website, not on card design.<ref name="pcf-5457-77503">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=77503#77503 A Question for the masses.], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (17 May 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618064410/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=5457&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=20 Internet Archive]</ref> On 15 July 2005 he posted "A Recap and more questions", a list of the players' requests with the PC's status on each. Among other points, the main page was being updated two to three times a week; the old Collecting thread had been lost; Decipher's card lists were available through Ruddog while the PC looked into whether it could host them; and [[Virtual Set 10: Fourth Anthology|Virtual Set 10]] had cards, such as the Shocks, meant to slow the game. Answering a request for more cash tournaments, he wrote that he had won the New York State Championship ([[2005 New York State Championship]]) and split about $200 with another player.<ref name="pcf-6375-88430" /> In October 2005 he wrote that the PC did not have $150,000, the cost that the makers of an online card game had given him, when he spoke to them personally, for setting up a supported Star Wars version;<ref name="pcf-7316-103486">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=103486#103486 Tournament Related Stuff], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (10 October 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618000417/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=7316&start=0 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-7316-103490">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=103490#103490 Tournament Related Stuff], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (10 October 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618000417/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=7316&start=0 Internet Archive]</ref> in February 2006 he named them as the makers of the online Lord of the Rings game.<ref name="pcf-7316-122820">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=122820#122820 Tournament Related Stuff], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (1 February 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618000417/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=7316&start=0 Internet Archive]</ref> In December 2005 he reposted in the forum's Trade/Collecting Questions thread pages that had been saved from the old collecting thread.<ref name="pcf-5796-113113">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=113113#113113 Trade/Collecting Questions], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 December 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618084301/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=5796&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=100 Internet Archive]</ref>

On 23 May 2006 he added the errata sheet and the [[Virtual Set 11: Gathering Storm|Virtual Set 11]] preview cards to the swccgpc.com main page.<ref name="pcf-10024-138374">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=138374#138374 virtual set update on the main page], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (23 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617234636/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10024&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref> When the PC released errata on 12 June 2006, he explained that the new Sim Aloo followed a future theme of the Imperial Council and the disbanding of the Senate, that Influence was a characteristic of certain characters related to the Imperial Council, and that the [Maintenance] icon targeted maintenance cards;<ref name="pcf-10265-140671">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=140671#140671 YOU CANNOT BE SERIOUS?!!!  NOW?!], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618100958/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10265&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=0 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-10265-140700">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=140700#140700 YOU CANNOT BE SERIOUS?!!!  NOW?!], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (12 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618100932/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=10265&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=20 Internet Archive]</ref> on 13 June he announced a PDF of the 13 cards being errata'd early, to which the three buddy effects and [[No Questions Asked (V)]] had been added.<ref name="pcf-10285-140943">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=140943#140943 Errata PDF], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618093001/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=140948&highlight= Internet Archive]</ref>

In May 2006 Lingrell was the contact for a Players Committee call for volunteers for its Writing Team, a Graphic Designer and an Intern.<ref name="pc-sid8">[http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=8 Volunteers Needed], swccgpc.com (23 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617220108/http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=8 Internet Archive]</ref> On Friday 26 May 2006, from 5 to 6 pm, he held a design Q&A on the new Redux set and the Re-Edit.<ref name="pc-news2006">[http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&new_topic Scott Lingrell - Design Q & A Friday 5/26 5-6pm], swccgpc.com news (18 May 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060617220030/http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&new_topic Internet Archive]</ref> In August 2006, after the design team discussed card availability with [[Michael Bahr]] and [[Jim Colson]], Lingrell asked Bahr for a list of cards the PC should avoid virtualizing; Bahr's work became the Virtualization Market Guide. In August 2008 Lingrell explained the PC's virtualization policy based on that guide (see [[Virtual cards#Virtualization Market Guide|Virtual cards]]).<ref name="pc-sid94">[http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=94 Policy of virtualizing], swccgpc.com (15 August 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080906211140/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=94 Internet Archive]</ref> When [[Virtual Set 15: Galactic Frontier|Virtual Set 15]] came up, he told its design team what was planned: "We're going back to Tatooine."<ref name="pc-sid81">[http://www.swccgpc.com/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=81 Virtual Set 15 - Galactic Frontier], swccgpc.com (28 March 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080712072006/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=81 Internet Archive]</ref>

In "10 Questions with Scott Lingrell", posted on 8 October 2008, the interviewer gave Lingrell's official title as Design Advocate. Lingrell said he had been on the playtesting team, and was asked to help out when Eric was leaving design; from there he helped in more and more areas, and he saw himself as "the public face of the game". Over the previous year and a half he had begun delegating, bringing more volunteers in to share the work.<ref name="pc-news7" /> He credited [[Michael Bahr|Mike Bahr]] and others for what the PC had learned about design, Evan and [[Nick Kolnik]] for improving the forums, [[Jerry Jensen]] for the templates used to make the PDFs, and Dennis and JW for PDFs with the actual Decipher images. He said [[Jason Robinette]] had originally designed the PC's logo, PDFs and website from scratch.<ref name="pc-news7" /> He named the design process, the advanced rulebook, the new website and ratings, starting with the [[2008 World Championship]], as the keys to bringing the game to where it was. He looked forward to a convention presence and a [[2009 Match Play Championship|Match Play Championship]] at a hotel in 2009, and hoped to start a planned giving program by 2012, so that people could leave money in their estate plans to help ensure the future of the game.<ref name="pc-news7">[http://www.swccgpc.com/news/news.php?id=7 10 Questions with Scott Lingrell], swccgpc.com (8 October 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081009225918/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/news/news.php?id=7 Internet Archive]</ref>

On 30 August 2008, answering a suggestion by [[James Booker]], Lingrell agreed that the World Champion would be the #1 seed at the [[2009 Match Play Championship|Match Play Championship]].<ref name="pcf-22721-332543">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=332543#332543 #1 seed], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 August 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080913050409/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=332582&sid=49360ecb005b2a8b076275625efc78a5 Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-22721-329434">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=329434#329434 #1 seed], James Booker, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (21 August 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080913050409/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=332582&sid=49360ecb005b2a8b076275625efc78a5 Internet Archive]</ref> On 30 September 2008 he posted the venue, the Holiday Inn in Cherry Hill, New Jersey, for 3–4 January 2009.<ref name="pcf-23352-338456">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=338456#338456 Hotel Information], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (30 September 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081201191120/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=338456&sid=cf267b31e64f04c5a0f5a2eee27ef5e7 Internet Archive]</ref> On 15 October 2008 he announced that, after talks with the players in charge of the Match Play Championship, two separate events would be run: MPC 2009 on 3–4 January in Open constructed format, and a Players Championship in March 2009 in Worlds 2000 format with $1,000 guaranteed to the winner. The top 4 of each event would meet in an eight-player event at Origins or Gen Con, whose winner would get $500.<ref name="pcf-23548-341470">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=341470#341470 Player's Championship - March 2008, Worlds 2000 Format], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 October 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081021233924/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=342143&sid=198be8cdf7bda3b05cc740ccf203ad9f Internet Archive]</ref> In November 2008 he wrote that Philipp was working on letting ratings be updated by event date rather than submission date, so that Worlds events would be calculated correctly.<ref name="pcf-24063-350899">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=350899#350899 Tournament Tutorial (Ratings Info)], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (17 November 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207045338/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=355072&sid=da800f192a94d4e0badb0ea8628c4ff7 Internet Archive]</ref> In December 2008 he kept the Match Play Championship preregistration list and expected the event to pass the previous year's turnout, which he recalled as 44.<ref name="pcf-22347-357623">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=357623#357623 Preregistration List - 38], Scott Lingrell, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 December 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207045353/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=357261&sid=da800f192a94d4e0badb0ea8628c4ff7 Internet Archive]</ref>

He organized the [[2006 New Jersey State Championship]] on Saturday 24 June 2006 at the Lawrenceville Public Library in Lawrenceville, New Jersey ($10 entry, $100 cash to first place), announcing it from the Players Committee's Advocate forum account.<ref name="sf-10071-140284">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=140284#p140284 NJ States - June 24th, 2006], Advocate, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (8 June 2006). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125175727/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t19288-start120.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="sf-20608-296728">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=296728#p296728 Texas MPC 08 - Saturday Deck Choices], Advocate, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (27 April 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125182426/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t20608.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="sf-20608-296865">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=296865#p296865 Texas MPC 08 - Saturday Deck Choices], The Franchise (Brad Eier), Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (27 April 2008). == Card credits ==
The printed credit lines of 7 [[Players Committee]] [[Virtual cards|Virtual card]]s name Scott Lingrell (7 original concept credits).<ref name="labels">[https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/src/gemp-swccg-cards/src/main/resources/card_labels.json card_labels.json] in billbisco/swccg-gemp (commit 0bc4377d9): the printed labels of every Players Committee Virtual card, transcribed from the PC's card images. Field definitions: [https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/docs/card_labels.md docs/card_labels.md].</ref> The credited cards are in [[Virtual Block 5]], [[Virtual Set 1]], [[Virtual Set 16]], [[Virtual Set 17]] and [[Virtual Set 25]], sets dated 2009–2025 on this wiki. The events named in the concept credits date from 2003 to 2004. The concept credits also name the event or award the concept came from: Mystic Visions Winner 2004 ([[2004 Mystic Visions]]; 1 card); Playtest Contest Winner 2003 (1 card). The full list of everyone credited is at [[Card Credits#Scott Lingrell|Card Credits]].
